mentions.title: Pagliacci is a classic with reliable pizza that works in a pinch

factorSources.note: The Infatuation (Aimee Rizzo) scores Humble Pie an 8.0, calling the wood-fired pizzas excellent and highlighting the classic margherita and the meat-heavy 'whole hog,' while praising the eco-conscious patio setting next to a chicken coop.

The Infatuation rates it 7.2, calling it a solid New York-style slice joint with a notably spicy red sauce, good for soaking up a late Capitol Hill night; Seattle Spectator's head-to-head slice comparison scored it lower (6/10), finding the sampled pepperoni slice greasy and soggy despite acceptable crust and flavor.

The Stranger's David Schmader recommends Ballard Pizza Company, writing that its inventive house pies rise to 'destination restaurant' level while custom pies are merely good, 'on par with Piecora's'; The Infatuation similarly calls it one of the closest things to New York-style pizza west of the Mississippi, singling out the rotating daily slices.

The Infatuation scores Slice Box 8.5, praising the New York-style pies' crispy crust and calling the cheese slice 'an instant classic,' with the thick Sicilian pepperoni square singled out as the one to prioritize.

The Infatuation calls Pagliacci 'a classic with reliable pizza that works in a pinch,' valuing its crushed-tomato base for group orders; longtime Seattle Times critic John Hinterberger's 1996 review rated it among the best pizza in Seattle, praising a crust that's 'springy and chewy without being tough or coarse.'
